title: S.F. Democratic Party stands behind Flock surveillance cameras in sweeping vote
summary: The San Francisco Democratic County Central Committee voted 11-3 (with 4 abstentions) to affirm support for the city's Flock ALPR cameras, rejecting a competing resolution by Gordon Mar that would have called for stricter guardrails and possible contract suspension. Two committee members who work for Flock were allowed to vote despite conflict-of-interest concerns. The Board of Supervisors may decide on renewing the city's Flock contract in February 2027.

key_quotes.quote: Both sides acknowledged that the city's Flock camera data was illegally accessed more than 1.6 million times in 2024 and 2025, with lots of those searches reaching out-of-state agencies like ICE.
Two of the committee's current members — Lily Ho and Trevor Chandler — work for Flock.
In February 2027, however, the Board of Supervisors may decide whether to renew the city's Flock contract.
